recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-5186; if PA wants to rename Patient.link.other in the future, handle it as a separate breaking-change proposal rather than as an unapplied part of this Person issue.
issue_request: FHIR-5186 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 Patient Administration change request for Person and RelatedPerson. The ballot comment said Person should not use the element name "other" because Other was itself a FHIR resource name; the final resolution said the property would be changed to "Target" and only noted that Patient link "Other" should be considered separately for consistency.
initial_application: The request appears to have been applied by dc2afae9f6e31b220e90a9d948c46e3743363e68, a grouped Person ballot reconciliation commit explicitly listing tracker 5186. That commit changed the Person spreadsheet from Person.link.other to Person.link.target, added Person example links using target, and added target-based Person search definitions; later source refactors migrated this into the current StructureDefinition and search-parameter bundle.
additional_context: Person, Patient, and RelatedPerson are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. Current Person conformance source, examples, and search parameters consistently use Person.link.target. Patient.link.other remains a separate Patient-specific element for another Patient or RelatedPerson, but FHIR-5186 did not finally approve renaming Patient.link.other, and current wording no longer invokes the retired Other resource name.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The authoritative current Person source already reflects the approved target rename across the element definition, examples, and search parameters; changing Patient.link.other would exceed the final seed decision and require a separate work-group decision.

related_jiras.note: Mentioned in the same historical grouped Person ballot reconciliation commit and already audited separately on the combined branch; it does not affect the FHIR-5186 target-rename decision.
